what: A census of every LINK TARGET (href / url / link props) present in stored page documents in production, per store, plus the block-by-block link map of the one document that is actually published. Targets and counts only, no tenant copy: the census records WHERE a document sends a visitor, never what it says.
why: The block census next door (scripts/stored-block-types.json) answers 'does every stored block still RESOLVE?'. Nothing answered the other half — 'does every stored link still GO anywhere?' — and on 2026-08-24 the answer turned out to be no, for every link in the corpus at once (ADR-1114). The home page is the case that matters: `/` is the site's root and the strongest page it has, and the published document that IS the home page (OWN-043) offers the visitor exactly ONE destination, which is a retired address.
howToRecapture: Run the SQL in `recaptureQuery` against production (read-only) and rewrite `stores` + `home` from the result, then set `capturedAt`. The CLASSIFICATION half is deliberately not captured: `retired` is re-derived from the redirect table in next.config.ts every time a probe reads this file, so retiring a new URL can turn a reading red without a re-capture.
scope: The Puck-shaped page documents only: pages.data (marketing drafts), pages.published_data (marketing published), and spaces.preferences.pageDocs / .puck (Space micro-sites). Chrome is deliberately OUT of scope — the header and footer menus are DB rows in `menus`, guarded by check:menu, and a visitor reaches them from every page rather than from a document.
recaptureLog: 2026-08-25 — RE-CAPTURED before working LIVE-104/108/109, because ADR-1082 requires a row's premise to be re-tested rather than believed. `recaptureQuery` was re-run against production and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 reading on every axis: same three stores, same 4/1/18 document counts, same 8/5/18 hrefs set, same 20/3/36 empty, same three targets at the same 7+1 / 4+1 / 18 hit counts. No premise had expired. The date moves; not one number does. ⚠️ The reading still describes production BEFORE supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql is applied — the file is deliberately unapplied (ADR-1125), so this census stays red on purpose and MUST be re-captured after the owner applies it. Re-capturing before the apply would record a fix that has not happened.

2026-08-25 (second recapture, LIVE-115 pass): 🔴 THE PREVIOUS ENTRY STAMPED capturedAt 2026-08-25 WHILE THE BODY STILL HELD THE 2026-08-24 READING. That is exactly the failure HYG-023 predicts — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it, and three probes (LIVE-104/108/109) went on agreeing with 'open' from a snapshot that no longer described production. Re-read live and the corpus is almost entirely clean: /onboarding/beta is GONE from every store, no navigation link hardcodes the site origin, and the 18 Space documents now point at #contact rather than '#'. What remains is the home page's ONE destination.

2026-09-07 (HYG-023, ADR-1241): RE-CAPTURED while building the checker, because the checker's first run against the file found exactly what the entry above predicts. The `home` block map had been re-captured when LIVE-104 closed (8 links, 4 destinations, verified identical to production today), but `stores` had NOT: pages.published_data still said 5 set hrefs all /join, so the census named three links its own store did not know. Re-read live: pages.data 4 documents / 11 set / 17 empty (/join x8 across 4, plus the home draft's /about, /discover, /how-to-start-a-circle); pages.published_data 1 / 8 / 0 (the block map, hit for hit); spaces.preferences.pageDocs 19 / 16 / 41 (#contact x16 in 16 documents; three newer Spaces carry only the empty seeded ctaHref). Zero retired, zero origin-pinned. From this entry on, scripts/check-stored-links.mjs requires capturedAt to be the date of the newest entry here, so a date can no longer move on its own.
recaptureQuery: with docs as (select 'pages.data' as store, slug as doc_key, data as doc from pages where data is not null union all select 'pages.published_data', slug, published_data from pages where published_data is not null union all select 'spaces.preferences.puck', slug, preferences->'puck' from spaces where preferences ? 'puck' union all select 'spaces.preferences.pageDocs', s.slug||'#'||d.key, d.value from spaces s, lateral jsonb_each(coalesce(s.preferences->'pageDocs','{}'::jsonb)) d), items as (select store, doc_key, e as blk from docs, lateral jsonb_array_elements(doc->'content') e where jsonb_typeof(doc->'content')='array'), hrefs as (select store, doc_key, blk->>'type' as type, k as prop, v #>> '{}' as href from items, lateral jsonb_each(blk->'props') as p(k,v) where jsonb_typeof(v)='string' and (k ilike '%href%' or k ilike '%url%' or k ilike '%link%')) select store, doc_key, href, count(*) as n from hrefs where href <> '' group by store, doc_key, href order by store, doc_key, href;

stores.note: The marketing DRAFT documents. ✅ WAS the worst store: four documents, every set href at /onboarding/beta. Now four documents carry a link prop and every set href is live: /join in all four, plus the home draft's /about, /discover and /how-to-start-a-circle (the draft is byte-identical to the published document, LIVE-104).

The marketing PUBLISHED documents. `home` is the only page ever published and by OWN-043 it IS the home page: app/page.tsx renders it and nothing else. Eight set hrefs, none empty, four destinations. This store holds ONE document, so check-stored-links.mjs requires these targets to equal the `home` block map hit for hit.

The Space micro-site documents, at preferences.pageDocs.home.content. ✅ Every SET href points at #contact, the in-page SpaceContact section (which renders inside <section id="contact">, the anchor lib/spaces/section-anchors.ts names canonically). Zero carry '#'. Nineteen documents carry a link prop; sixteen set it to #contact and three newer Spaces carry only the empty seeded value, because the template seeds ctaHref empty and SpaceCalloutBlock requires BOTH a label and a destination, so a new Space draws no button until its operator points it somewhere.

chromeForReference.headerBehindJs: The Community / The Quest / Spaces / About are <button> mega triggers, not links. Their 19 panel items (menus.surface_key='header') exist only after hydration, so a crawler and a no-JS visitor never reach /discover, /pricing, /the-community, /the-quest, /spaces, /help or /what-is-frequency from `/`.
